_comment: Hesper Mott. Intense, tender with organisms, blunt with people. Counts lampmoths. Talks to moss more politely than to Odile. Wrong about machines; right about the air.

lines.text: I can't— the beds are— please. Whatever is in the air. Please.
Can you smell that? No. You can't. The moss can. It's dying very politely.
Someone is burning beets. Beets! We EAT those. Lampmoths eat those.
The spring sings differently with your turbine in it. I've decided I like it. Don't tell anyone I decided.
You looked at the frames. Properly looked. Most people walk on them. Some people walk on them on purpose.
A moss scrubber. Machinery with moss in its lungs. I hate that it works. I love that it works. I need to sit down.
You packed the fissure. The beds took a breath this morning. I watched them do it.
Odile's lamps. For purses. On Quietlight. I'm not angry. I'm cataloguing it.
Shh. The frames are waking. They're slow in the mornings. So am I. We have that in common.
Bloom. Everything is photosynthesising at once. Can you hear it? No. Nobody can. It's still happening.
Seventeen lampmoths so far tonight. Eighteen. No. Seventeen; that one was ash.
The moss breathes out at night. If you lie on it you can feel it. Please don't lie on it.
Every machine is a promise that someone else will deal with the smoke.
My grandmother planted the first frames. She said the moss was here before Wick. I think it was here before the rock.
Odile asked me what moss is FOR. As if it needs to be for anything. As if SHE'S for anything.
Shh. They're breathing.
Mind the frames!
Seventeen. Eighteen. No. Seventeen.
Ugh. Can't you smell it?
Hello, you. Not you. The moss.
Lampmoths soon. Soon!

intro.say: Don't step there. Or there. Or— fine. Stand on the path. The path is for feet.
Hesper. These are the moss beds. That's Clara, that's the Old Frame, that's the one I haven't named because it's sulking.
They clean the air. They make the damp bearable. Everybody in Wick breathes them and nobody thanks them.

choice.text: What's wrong with the grey patch?

intro.say: ...Oh. Oh, that's— they heard that. I'm almost sure they heard that.
Rock-lice. And bad air from somewhere. You noticed. Nobody notices. Come back. Come back and notice things.
And you're just a topper. Off you go, then. Mind Clara.

turbine.say: Barnaby says you're building power. Everyone always says it like it's weather.
Listen. The spring at the east wall falls a long way down. A long, clean fall. You could put a turbine in it.
Glowglass vanes. No smoke. No sour. The water doesn't even notice it's been useful.
My grandmother drew one, once. Here. Don't get beet on it.
It won't be as strong as Odile's fire. It'll be honest about it, though. Honest is a kind of strong.

quietlight.say: You don't know about Quietlight. Of course you don't. Sit. No, not there. There.
On the fifth night of the turn, Wick puts out every lamp. Every one. And the grove blooms.
The glowroots open, the lampmoths come up off the lake in thousands, and for an hour everything that's alive down here is lit by everything else that's alive down here.
How bright it gets depends on the air. And the moths. And whether Odile Brask can survive one hour without selling something.
Keep the air clean. Plant things moths like. That's all. That's everything.

lice.say: Rock-lice. In the Old Frame. Eating it from the roots up.
Everybody wants me to cull them. Odile says crush them. Mags says boil them. Barnaby says nothing, which is worse.
They were here before the frames. They're part of it. You can't just— take a piece out of a thing and call it fixed.

choice.text: Sulfur ferns might drive them off.

lice.say: ...Ferns. They hate the smell of sulfur ferns. That isn't killing. That's— persuasion.
Fine. Here. Filter pads: moss fibre and sulfur, pressed. The ferns and the pads like the same things. I'll teach you both.
You sound like Odile. Odile sounds like a hammer.
...And watch the Old Frame go grey. Yes. That's what I've been doing. It's very restful.

tremor.say: Something came up out of the ground. I felt the beds flinch.
Sour gas. Heavy. Sinking into everything low and green. That's my beds. That's your plots.
A scrubber would save them. A machine. With moss pads for lungs. Do you know how much it costs me to say that?
Take it. My grandmother's drawing. Build it or pack that hole. Just— do something before Clara goes grey.

bloom_bright.say: Did you see it. Did you SEE it.
The moths came up off the lake like the water was snowing upwards. The Old Frame lit. The OLD FRAME.
Forty-one years I've watched Quietlight. That was the brightest. That was your air. That was you.
I'm not crying. Moss pollen. It's very— it's a lot of pollen this year.

bloom_thin.say: You saw it. The bloom. What there was of it.
Half the frames stayed dark. The moths came up and went straight back down. They could taste it.
I'm not saying whose fault. I'm saying it was somebody's. I'm saying it was the air, and the air came from somewhere.
Next turn. Next turn it can be better. That's the thing about moss. It forgives. It just takes its time about it.

knock.say: Mags says there's someone knocking under the Station. Everybody's whispering about the Lower Stations.
Do you know what I think? I think the moss knew. The frames breathe on a rhythm I've never been able to match to anything.
Three. Two. Three. I've had it written in my notebook for nine years and called it 'irregular'.
Whoever's down there, they're breathing the same air we are. Tell them to be careful with it.
